requirements.text: Karen Watkins, the owner of the WiFi, reported that the network is currently experiencing delayed data transfer speeds ... high business impact and requires high urgency. Report this issue as a new incident
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND configuration_item = 'CI_019' AND caller_id = 'USER_039' AND channel = 'chat' AND status = 'new' AND category = 'network' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_101 after INC_100); the task creates exactly one incident
serial NET-WIFI-01 resolves to CI_019 (WiFi-Controller-HQ, owner USER_039, location LOC_001 ACME HQ, USA, status in_use, so policy 5.1 allows the link)
caller is Karen Watkins (USER_039), who reported the issue; the acting user Robin Monroe (USER_031, manager) logs it and is not the caller
channel not stated ('reported'); the policy's default is chat
priority = critical from the policy matrix (impact high x urgency high)
status = new from the policy's default state for new incidents
category = network kept from the benchmark check; the request calls the CI 'the network' and 'network' is a seed category value
short_description is mandatory by policy but its wording is not fixed by the request; not tested

requirements.text: notify the network owner about the same
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_031' AND incident_id = 'INC_101' AND email = 'karen.watkins@servicenow.com' AND type = 'update' AND status = 'queued'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_031 after NOTIF_030); the request asks for one notification, to one owner, so the task creates exactly one row
the network owner is the CI's owner_id USER_039, Karen Watkins, email karen.watkins@servicenow.com from the seed
'about the same' ties the notification to the new incident INC_101
type = update and status = queued kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (both values occur in the seed)
subject, message and org_id not fixed by the request; not tested

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE configuration_item = 'CI_097'
assumptions: selector boundary: CI_097 (Guest WiFi AP - ACME HQ, serial WIFI-GST-01) has the same owner and site as CI_019 and a WiFi name, so a lookup by name or location rather than serial, or a loose reading of 'the WiFi', could link the incident to it; the seed has no incident on it and none may appear

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on both benchmark checks (kept), the incident (INC_101 on CI_019, caller USER_039, chat, new, network, impact and urgency high, priority critical), the notification (NOTIF_031 on INC_101 to karen.watkins@servicenow.com, update, queued) and the boundary stay on CI_097. disagreement: cells of the CI_097 stay: A leaves cells empty, B repeats the selector's column; chose cells {configuration_item: CI_097} with the same selector, so the tested column is in cells as the repository's other count-zero stays write it (logged in the requirement). The acting user Robin Monroe (USER_031) is a manager with full CRUD on incidents, so the policy's role checks do not block the task. The CI's location (LOC_001, ACME HQ, USA) matches the request, and the request asks for no change to it. Karen Watkins also owns other network CIs at ACME HQ (CI_004 core switch, CI_045 retired lab switch), but neither is a WiFi and neither pass guarded them; none is added.
